artifacts.summary: 9-phase, 10.5-hour sequential plan burning nolints.json 307 -> 217 (unusedArguments grandfathered on evidence) and dupNamespace 14 -> 0, with per-category jq removal proved by green runLinter and a policy/comment refresh phase.

memory_candidates.content: Pattern for planning a linter-suppression-baseline burndown (Batteries nolints.json, and structurally the same for any mypy/eslint/ruff baseline file): never regenerate the baseline wholesale with the tool's own --update flag, because --update rewrites the file from CURRENT findings and silently grandfathers any genuine regression introduced by the same edit. Instead, phase the work one linter category at a time, and in each phase (a) fix every finding in that category, (b) remove exactly that category from the baseline with a filter (jq 'map(select(.[0] == "CATEGORY" | not))' -- the '| not' form, not '!=', per the jq-escaping workaround), and (c) require a green run of the linter driver as the phase gate. Step (c) is the load-bearing part: an exit-0 driver run with the category absent from the baseline proves both that the category is genuinely fixed AND that no new finding appeared, which a wholesale regenerate can never prove. Corollary for phase sizing: categories that are legitimately permanent (e.g. typeclass parameters retained for signature uniformity across a family) should be grandfathered with a WRITTEN, measured rationale in a project doc rather than burned down -- and that rationale is itself a plan phase, not a footnote.
